name: Kill Holiday
label: Revelation
lede: Two Unbroken members, Steven Miller and Rob Moran, traded San Diego's metallic hardcore for long, moody indie rock. Four releases later, Revelation put out the seven-minute songs.

eras.title: A side road off Unbroken
eras.text: Unbroken were among San Diego's heaviest hardcore bands. Kill Holiday started in that band's last year and a half, when guitarist-singer Steven Miller and bassist Rob Moran went somewhere slower, cutting every early single at Doubletime Studio with engineer Jeff Forrest.

years.h: Unbroken's Steven Miller and Rob Moran start a band in a car
years.p: Miller sings and plays guitar, Moran plays bass, Oscar Paz is on guitar and Barry Kellman on drums. The band plays indie rock and punk, not Unbroken's metallic hardcore.
years.xp:
Miller told No Echo the band formed during Unbroken's final year and a half, "purely by chance": he was riding in a car with Moran and Kellman while they talked about starting something.

It was also Miller's first time fronting a band on record. He said Monitor Dependency was "my first time ever singing on a recording", backup vocals in Julia aside.

years.h: One day at Doubletime, two songs for New Age
years.p: Monitor Dependency is recorded March 27, 1995, with Jeff Forrest. The 7" on New Age Records has Monitor Dependency and Cold Shoulder.

years.h: Dempsey and Kill Holiday split a 7" on Indecision
years.p: Agenda and Sugar Rush are the Kill Holiday side: 274 copies on yellow vinyl, 353 on black. Rob Moran has left and June Cate is in.

years.cap: Flyer for Kill Holiday and Tristeza at Espresso Roma Cafe, San Diego, October 25, 1997
years.src: No Echo: Steven Miller · Discogs: Meant To Let You Down
yt: Meant to Let You Down (fan upload)
years.h: Meant To Let You Down comes out on Simba
years.p: Recorded July 20, 1997, with Todd Beattie on bass. [[Gabriel Gamboa|bc189271-5c40-40e0-bcd5-0f29cfa1c6f7]] shoots the photos and does the layout, a year before he takes over the drums.
years.xp:
Miller said his singing improved on this record because the band was "playing out a lot" and he was "becoming comfortable with singing."

The credits list the drummer as "Barry Holiday", presumably Kellman under a stage name.

eras.title: Seven minutes is the short version
eras.text: The one album stretched out to ten songs, several past seven minutes, with keyboards and noise. Revelation released it in 1999, and the band was done the next year.

years.cap: Kill Holiday at the Pickle Patch, circa 1998
years.h: Gamboa takes over drums, and the new record goes long
years.p: Miller, guitarist Christopher Perreira, Todd Beattie and Gabriel Gamboa, now on drums, cut the album with Jeff Forrest at Doubletime. Forrest adds keyboards and noises.
years.xp:
The change came when Kellman left. Miller said the sound shifted accidentally once Gamboa joined on drums.

Revelation had first shown interest with Kellman still in the band, and Miller said it "never really occurred to us" to tell the label the lineup and direction had changed.

years.src: Discogs: Somewhere Between the Wrong Is Right (Rev:77)
years.h: Somewhere Between the Wrong Is Right arrives on Revelation
years.p: Ten songs on Rev:77, with You're Taking It Well, Something Borrowed Something Blue and In Closing (Memorial Day) all past seven minutes. [[Jeff Caudill|6a41fff4-9b5c-4b1c-9ebf-4df434fdbbec]] of [[Gameface|c67fddd4-970b-4bfb-8996-314c29b08f27]] shot the cover and designed it.
years.xp: Two of the long ones are on YouTube as fan audio uploads: You're Taking It Well and Something Borrowed Something Blue.
play: Somewhere Between the Wrong Is Right

years.h: After six years and four releases, the band ends
years.p: Kill Holiday finish in 2000. Miller and Gamboa carry on in [[The Landslide|12c8eb9a-bcef-4cae-a45b-9861c41705b9]]; Moran later plays in [[Some Girls|ffee2206-eb9e-4b39-9447-8977e269ed0e]] and [[Narrows|3a9bf775-66f1-4299-b062-5cb0585d5672]].
years.xp: Miller told No Echo it was "starting to become exhausting." He also said he made a mistake by going "too deep lyrically" in dealing with the death of Eric Allen.

eras.title: Purple, seventeen years on
eras.text: Revelation put the album back on vinyl for Record Store Day.

years.h: Revelation presses 717 purple copies for Record Store Day
years.p: The April 16, 2016 reissue of Somewhere Between the Wrong Is Right comes with a lyric and credits sheet.
